verdict.rationale: VirtualPostMail's TruLease provides a one-year lease agreement, a physical address and an optional company-name utility bill, marketed for compliance with financial accounts and Amazon Store. The provider also states that a virtual mailbox address does not work for opening bank accounts and that only TruLease or TruResidence can provide the proof needed. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on evidence that banks and payment processors actually accept the documents, explicit naming of payment processors or specific accepting institutions, and the utility bill being a paid add-on rather than included.

support.subject: As a founder, I can get documentation that banks and payment processors accept as proof of business address, with the provider stating where the address works and where it doesn't

citations.quote: Establish a business location by renting a commercial office space backed by a lease agreement, physical address, and utility service to meet compliance requirements for financial accounts, Amazon Store, and more.
TruLease helps you obtain the essential documentation you need to meet address verification and compliance requirements without the headaches of a traditional office lease.
When renting an office, you'll sign a one-year lease agreement that verifies your business has legal rights to the office space.
A virtual mailbox works for receiving mail, but not for activities like opening bank accounts. These actions often require proof of physical presence, which only TruLease or TruResidence can provide.
For an additional fee, you can set up utility service (landline or Internet) under your company’s name.
